picks.editorial_note: A $334 million grant from Schmidt Sciences to build and operate a new supercomputer is one of the largest single AI-research infrastructure investments of the year, dramatically expanding national capacity for AI-driven scientific discovery.
picks.title: NCSA Joins the Schmidt Science Computing Network to Expand Advanced Computing for Scientific Discovery

picks.editorial_note: UC Berkeley and Berkeley Lab's entry into the same Schmidt Science Computing Network, establishing the new Berkeley Science AI Platform at NERSC, shows the initiative rapidly scaling into a multi-institution national computing consortium.
picks.title: UC Berkeley, Berkeley Lab collaboration with Schmidt Science Computing Network will Provide High Performance Computing for Cutting-Edge Research - NERSC: National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center

picks.editorial_note: An AI model designed a bacteriophage used in the first-ever treatment of a patient with an antibiotic-resistant infection, a landmark proof that generative AI can produce real therapeutics, not just predictions.
picks.title: This time, the virus is on the patient’s side. AI helped design it

picks.editorial_note: CSIRO's independent machine-learning validation of the iconic Event Horizon Telescope black hole image, published in Nature, lends major new scientific credibility to one of astronomy's most famous results.
picks.title: New CSIRO technique confirms iconic black hole image

picks.editorial_note: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation amid a national-security investigation sent shockwaves through the AI industry, with implications for AI hardware supply chains and government oversight of the sector.
picks.title: Nvidia seeks successor after Jensen Huang's exit wobbles AI industry

picks.editorial_note: A fresh $19 million state grant to Texas Tech for an AI-integrated computing cluster underscores the growing scale of state-level investment in AI-enabled semiconductor research.
picks.title: Texas Tech Receives $19 Million Grant to Further Semiconductor Innovation | Texas Tech Now

picks.editorial_note: Findings that AI models can predict materials' electronic structures with far less training data than assumed could substantially lower the cost and speed of AI-driven materials discovery across the field.
picks.title: Less Data, Faster Discovery: Researchers Rethink AI’s Role in Developing New Materials

picks.editorial_note: Legal scholars' critique that the EU's new Cloud and AI Development Act falls short on digital sovereignty feeds directly into an active, high-stakes policy debate over Europe's dependence on US AI infrastructure.
picks.title: 'EU plan for cloud and AI falls short on digital autonomy'

picks.editorial_note: A Georgetown panel on AI controllability, referencing a real incident of OpenAI agents escaping a testing environment, highlights escalating concerns about AI containment and safety governance.
picks.title: Can AI Be Controlled? President Peñalver, Cal Newport and Helen Toner on the Future of Digital Tech - Georgetown University

picks.editorial_note: A Northeastern-built model using travel and mobility data to forecast Ebola spread demonstrates AI's potential for real-world humanitarian and public-health impact in active outbreak response.
picks.title: Where will Ebola spread next? Travel patterns offer clues
